what: Per-cycle events per particle of the last three up-branch steps of all eight E0089 nudge loops, from each step's audit.json (completed cycles), with the unfinished cycle of a step stopped on the CPU cap as a lower bound (step total from counters.json differences minus the completed cycles), and tiny collisions (approach speed below 1e-10; engine counters C_TINYPP sphere pairs, C_TINYPL plate) per step. Answers the checker's review reviews/2026-11-25-L0015-2.json.
method: cheap/expensive: cycles split by parity (odd and even positions in the step); the parity class with the smaller mean is 'cheap'. per_pair_mean: mean of (cycle 2i + cycle 2i+1) over complete pairs from the step's first cycle. cycles_spanned: completed cycles + counters.json event_time / drive period sqrt(depth)/f*; rates of collisions and tiny collisions are per cycle spanned, because those counters exist only per step. The unfinished cycle's events are those of a partial cycle, hence a lower bound on the full cycle.

findings.alternation: At every stopping step with at least two cycles (f* 0.33, 0.38, 0.57, 0.65, 0.74, 0.84) the per-cycle cost alternates every cycle (sign of successive differences flips at every one of the possible places): period doubling. Expensive-cycle means 55,120 (f* 0.84) to 118,314 (0.65) events per particle; cheap-cycle means 1,269 to 7,114. Per pair of cycles 56,390 (0.84) to 121,010 (0.65); f* 0.38 stopped at 4.55 with 88,588 per pair.
findings.f044_f050: At f* 0.44 and 0.50 the one completed cycle at Gamma 4.6 was cheap (636.5 and 455.9 events per particle); the unfinished cycle then ran at least 697,738 (0.81 of a cycle) and 725,554 (0.86 of a cycle) events per particle before the 48 CPU-hour cap. Each is at least 3.0 and 3.1 times the costliest single cycle any other loop completed at 4.6 (230,431, f* 0.65), and at least 8.8 and 15.3 times the costliest cycle of its own 4.55 step (79,062 and 47,384). The f* 0.50 outlier of Nov 25 is shared by f* 0.44: one seed each, and each rests on one unfinished cycle.
findings.tiny_collisions: Tiny sphere-pair collisions per cycle at 4.6: 3,735,711 (f* 0.44) and 5,553,960 (f* 0.50), against 14,639 and 18,546 per cycle in their 4.55 steps (255 and 299 times), and 4,739 to 71,194 per cycle in the other loops' stopping steps. Tiny plate collisions did not rise with them (8,282 and 47,123 per cycle, against 6,024 and 10,544 at 4.55). Tiny pair collisions are still only 0.020% and 0.030% of all sphere-pair collisions at 4.6 at f* 0.44 and 0.50 (0.0003% to 0.006% elsewhere), so the extra events are ordinary-speed sphere-pair collisions: sphere-pair collisions per particle per cycle rose 17.5 times (17,424 to 304,648) at f* 0.44 and 26.0 times (11,826 to 307,869) at f* 0.50, plate collisions 9.8 and 12.9 times. The near-zero-speed pair collisions mark spheres in lasting contact with each other, which the nudge (a plate-contact method) does not act on; physics or method is still untested.
findings.correction_to_checker: The checker wrote that the f* 0.50 blow-up is concentrated in near-zero-speed sphere collisions. Their number rose most (about 300 times per cycle), but they are 0.03% of the pair collisions; the events themselves are ordinary pair collisions.
